title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals: Filing an Appeal and Timeliness
content:
An appeal under Unemployment Insurance Appeals must be in writing and filed through the online portal, by mail or by fax; a request made only by phone is not an appeal, and there is no filing fee. An appeal is timely only when it is filed no later than the filing deadline after the mailing date of the appealed determination or decision. The deadline is counted in calendar days starting the day after the mailing date; when the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or state holiday the deadline moves to the next business day, and the filing date is the postmark, fax or online submission date. A late appeal is still filed when the appellant states good cause as its late-filing reason, and it is heard on good cause and the merits together; a late appeal filed after the late appeal limit, or with no good cause stated, is dismissed as untimely. The appellant receives an acknowledgment with the docket number within the acknowledgment business days. While a claimant's appeal is pending the claimant must keep certifying each week where the docket requires it, or weeks won on appeal cannot be paid; an appeal of an overpayment determination suspends its recovery, and an employer appealing a contribution rate keeps paying at the appealed rate.

## The timeliness test, part by part

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| Event the clock starts from | the mailing date of the appealed determination or decision, as shown on the Department's record of that determination or decision |
| Length | the docket's filing deadline, in calendar days |
| Counting | day 1 is the day after the mailing date; every calendar day counts |
| Last day on a Saturday, Sunday or state holiday | the deadline moves to the next business day |
| Date compared | the filing date: the postmark, fax or online submission date |
| Direction and boundary | timely when the filing date is no later than the deadline; a filing on the last day of the deadline is timely |

The mailing date is read from the Department's record of the appealed determination or decision that the appeal names; the appellant's recollection of when the letter arrived does not replace it.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates and deadlines; no state holiday falls in the spans used)

1. *Last day on a weekday.* A determination is mailed on Monday 2 March 2026 and the deadline is 21 days. Day 1 is Tuesday 3 March; day 21 is Monday 23 March. An appeal postmarked 23 March is timely; one submitted online on Tuesday 24 March is late.
2. *Last day on a weekend.* A determination is mailed on Thursday 5 March 2026 and the deadline is 30 days. Day 30 is Saturday 4 April, so the deadline moves to Monday 6 April. A fax received on 6 April is timely; one sent on Tuesday 7 April is late.

## What follows from a late filing

| Filed after the deadline | Good cause stated as the late-filing reason | Within the late-appeal limit | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | filed; good cause and the merits are heard together |
| yes | no | — | dismissed as untimely |
| yes | — | no | dismissed as untimely |

## While the appeal is pending

- The claimant keeps certifying each week on a docket that requires it; otherwise weeks won on appeal cannot be paid.
- An appeal of an overpayment determination suspends recovery of that overpayment.
- An employer appealing a contribution rate keeps paying at the appealed rate.
